input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an MFN/right-to-match running against us: before engaging any other provider we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. It is open-ended — no defined product, no time limit, and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs — so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. We therefore take the preferred position and remove the obligation, leaving Section 7.2 as an express statement that we owe no disclosure or matching duty.

ops.oldText: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer has no obligation to disclose to Vendor, or to match for Vendor, any commercial offer it receives from another provider.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the obligation to disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit, as our playbook does not accept an MFN running against us; this also conforms Section 7.2 to Section 12.3, which confirms we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Replace the Customer-side disclose-and-match MFN in Section 7.2 with an express no-MFN statement.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
